blocks.heading: Your role
blocks.text: Run a museum gala, then lead the investigation into donor Grant Larceny’s death. You may play a character: nothing in this guide reveals which evidence letter any character uses or who becomes the murderer. Read the whole guide before printing.

blocks.heading: Object of the game
blocks.text: Before the confession, identify the murderer and explain their motive and how the evidence fits. Acting is welcome; reading the supplied answers is enough.

blocks.heading: Party details
blocks.text: October 30, 2026 / 1537 S 74th East Ave, Tulsa, OK 74112. Plan 6:00 arrival to 9:30 finish. Confirm all 15 core roles; add up to 15 optional roles.

blocks.heading: One week before
bullets: Confirm the guest list and assign character IDs. Include yourself if playing. Use the directory on pages 4–5.
Send each guest only their introduction PDF or PNG plus the invitation. Do not send the complete kit or a private packet.
Explain that costume suggestions are inspiration. Guests need no special item to satisfy an evidence clue.
Decide who reads announcements. A playing host can do it from this guide and the staged F cards.
Choose the actual rooms for the museum labels using page 8.

blocks.heading: Before guests arrive
bullets: Assemble the labeled play, EVIDENCE and FINALE envelopes using page 7.
Put F1–F5 in a closed host folder, ordered by number. Keep these separate from scavenger discoveries.
Hide discoveries 1–16; put blank ballots, pencils and question catalogs at seats.
Prepare the three animal bowls and a closed return box. No guest retains an animal slip.
Set an Evidence Table and quiet speaking area. Turn music down for seated rounds.
Leave the spoiler bible and source ZIP unopened if playing.

blocks.heading: Practical supplies
blocks.text: Printer, paper, scissors, envelopes, tape, timer and pens. Print at 100% actual size, single-sided. No font installation is needed. Test an open-freely page on your printer before the full run.

blocks.heading: Assign by personality
blocks.text: IDs 01–15 are the core cast; 16–30 are optional additions. Animals are drawn privately at arrival and are never assigned in this directory.

blocks.heading: At arrival / keep identities private
bullets: Each core guest draws from Player Bowl A. They read silently, memorize the animal, fold the slip and immediately drop it into the closed return box. They never keep it.
The next guest draws only from Bowl A, not the return box. Once all core arrivals have drawn, unused animals left in A identify absent players.
Remove those unused words from matching Murderer Bowl B. B now contains exactly the animals memorized by attending core guests.
Optional guests draw from the separate Optional Bowl, memorize and return their slips in the same way. Optional animals never enter B.
Do not record animal-to-name associations. Mix returned slips inside the closed box; put it away.

blocks.heading: Select after Act I
blocks.text: Ask everyone to keep a neutral face. Draw one animal from B without looking toward guests. Announce the word twice and write only that word on the host cue card. Do not ask who drew it.

blocks.heading: Say aloud
blocks.text: If you memorized [ANIMAL], you are the murderer. Use IF MURDERER from now on. Everyone else uses IF INNOCENT. Keep your animal and whether you are innocent or the murderer secret until the finale.

blocks.heading: Late arrival
blocks.text: Never redraw the murderer. A late core guest draws from the unused A animals already excluded from B; optional arrivals use their own bowl. They memorize, return the slip and play innocent.

blocks.heading: Per guest / match by ID and name
bullets: Print the four consecutive play pages from Secret_Individual. Keep them in order and label their PLAY envelope.
Cut both same-name cards from the evidence sheet. Seal both together in a separate EVIDENCE envelope. A/B letters do not consistently mean innocence or guilt.
Print that guest’s single FINALE page and seal it in a third, separately named envelope. Keep the confession out of the play packet.
Use 10_Blind_Printing_and_Assembly.pdf to match sheets 01–30 to names without reading the private text.
Print private documents face down, covering exposed pages. Use a non-playing printing helper if needed.
At check-in, give PLAY and EVIDENCE to the guest. Keep FINALE envelopes on a host tray until ballots are collected.

blocks.heading: Per seating pair
bullets: Supply a complete 11_Questions_and_Notes.pdf, not only its first page. Named questions are in ID order; bookmark the current guests.
Give each guest a pencil and blank ballot. Keep the host’s attendance/hearing roster separate.

blocks.heading: Host evidence folder
blocks.text: F1–F2: before Motive. F3: before Opportunity. F4–F5: before Method. Discoveries 1–16 belong in the room; the F reports do not.

blocks.heading: When a clue is found
blocks.text: Ask the finder to bring it to the Evidence Table and read it to nearby guests. Record finds for Curator’s Eye. Missing discoveries do not delay the seated investigation.

blocks.heading: Timing guidance
blocks.text: Budget 80 minutes for the three seated rounds with 30 guests. Keep each question/answer turn to about 40 seconds; Method needs about a minute with its receipt. With 15 guests, allow more discussion or finish earlier. Pause eating during spoken turns. These estimates still need a human rehearsal.

blocks.heading: Say aloud at arrival
blocks.text: Welcome to the Meridian Museum’s Treasures of the World gala. Grant Larceny expects gratitude, good manners and his name on absolutely everything. Open only the first page of your play packet. Introduce yourself, pursue your three tasks and explore the museum. Leave the later pages and your evidence envelope alone for now.

blocks.heading: Lead the opening
bullets: Invite each guest to say their character name and role. A sentence from the introduction is enough. Allow 15–20 seconds each.
Then let guests mingle in small groups. Their private tasks give them people and topics to seek out.
Encourage gossip about the donor’s decisions and found documents. Nobody has to invent an event or a private relationship.
Move quiet guests into a small conversation; they can read a task or introduction instead of performing.
At 6:55 call for buffet and ID-order seats. Mark attendance. Make sure every pair can reach a question catalog.

blocks.heading: Say aloud at the death
blocks.text: Grant Larceny has been found dead in the Donor Salon. His private cordial was poisoned. Please keep a neutral face while I draw the murderer’s animal.

blocks.heading: Then
blocks.text: Follow page 6’s animal announcement. Do not ask the selected guest to identify themselves. Move directly to Motive.

blocks.heading: Release
blocks.text: Read F1 / The private toast, then F2 / Grant’s unfinished business, verbatim from the staged report cards. Put both on the Evidence Table.

blocks.heading: Say aloud
blocks.text: Grant’s papers show that his generosity came with conditions. Some of you were about to lose money, work, reputation or an object you cared about. Turn to Round 1 / Motive. Ask the named Motive questions in the catalog. We need to hear from everyone.

blocks.heading: Run the question chain
bullets: Start with the lowest attending ID. The last seated guest asks that person’s named question from the catalog.
The respondent reads the answer for their role from the current page, then asks the next occupied seat their named question. Continue in order, skipping absent IDs.
Tick each answered ID on the roster. Everyone answers once. Labels stay private; only the speech box is read.
For a guest who prefers help, a neighbour may read the speech box they indicate. Do not ask which role they are using.

blocks.heading: Close the round
blocks.text: Ask pairs: Who stood to lose something? Which grievance sounds most urgent? Give two minutes to compare notes, then announce Opportunity. A motive alone is not a solution.

blocks.heading: Release
blocks.text: Read F3 / The salon door register verbatim. Display it beside F1–F2. Do not release F4 or F5 yet.

blocks.heading: Say aloud
blocks.text: We know when the drink was prepared and when Grant drank it. The door register tells us who could reach the service table between those events. Turn to Round 2 / Opportunity. Ask the named Opportunity questions, including the ordinary setup errands involving the cabinet key.

blocks.heading: Run the question chain
bullets: Start with the lowest attending ID. The last seated guest asks that person’s named question from the catalog.
The respondent reads the answer for their role from the current page, then asks the next occupied seat their named question. Continue in order, skipping absent IDs.
Tick each answered ID on the roster. Everyone answers once. Labels stay private; only the speech box is read.
For a guest who prefers help, a neighbour may read the speech box they indicate. Do not ask which role they are using.

blocks.heading: Close the round
blocks.text: Give pairs two minutes: Who visited after the drink was poured? What setup errands might matter? Keep several suspects under consideration. Then announce Method and ask everyone to wait while the next reports are read.

blocks.heading: Release
blocks.text: Read F4 / The missing conservation sample and F5 / A thread in the poison verbatim. Display both before anyone opens their EVIDENCE envelope.

blocks.heading: Say aloud
blocks.text: The cabinet key gave access to the missing sample. The poisoned linen smear tells us how it was applied. Several guests had ordinary reasons to borrow the key or carry that linen. Turn to Round 3 / Method. Open EVIDENCE and privately select the letter your page assigns. Leave the other card hidden.

blocks.heading: Collect and run
bullets: Collect one selected card per attending ID. Count against the roster and return it to its owner. The guest chooses the letter privately.
Use the same seat-order question chain. Ask each named Method question. The guest reads their selected speech, then the whole selected receipt.
Put each read receipt on the Evidence Table and tick that ID. Do not move on with a missing receipt.
Compare the door, key and linen findings in pairs. Name a suspect, motive and link between the reports.
Allow up to three challenges. A challenged guest can repeat their printed facts; no new factual alibi or object can be introduced.

blocks.heading: If discussion stalls
blocks.text: Ask: Which findings overlap? Does your suspect fit all the reports, or only one?

blocks.heading: Lock the decision
bullets: Give everyone a private ballot. Ask for suspect, motive and supporting evidence. The murderer votes too and may accuse another guest.
Collect every ballot before distributing FINALE envelopes. Once collected, no votes change.
Tally suspect votes. For Escaped Justice, include every positive-vote suspect tied at the third-place cutoff; zero-vote names never qualify.
Invite a few brief accusations while keeping the murderer’s identity secret. Do not read final statements yet.

blocks.heading: Say aloud
blocks.text: The ballots are locked. Whoever memorized [ANIMAL], please identify yourself. Open only your own FINALE envelope and read the confession. Everyone else leaves theirs sealed.

blocks.heading: After the confession
bullets: Master Sleuth: a ballot naming the murderer with their motive and a coherent link between the salon, key and linen evidence. Share the prize if reasoning is equally strong.
Escaped Justice: the murderer wins if outside the qualifying top-three suspects.
Best Actor and Best Costume: use ballot votes. Curator’s Eye: use the Act I discovery tally.
Offer dessert and debrief. Guests may now discuss their alternative branches.

blocks.heading: If something goes wrong
bullets: Forgotten animal before selection: quietly say so. Void the assignment round and restart for everyone, with no identity list. Never guess or borrow another guest’s word.
Forgotten animal after selection: stop. Never guess identity. Restart with fresh memorized assignments only if all core guests can do so; otherwise postpone scoring.
Wrong evidence card: the guest privately rechecks the IF INNOCENT / IF MURDERER line and swaps to their assigned letter before voting. Do not inspect their other branch.
Missing guest: skip their ID. Remove their unused animal before selection. A missing optional role cannot block an essential clue.
Someone reads ahead: stop them before any confession is spoken. FINALE remains on the host tray until ballots are locked.
Room drifting? Lower music, pause eating and resume the roster.
